lead: The Bible ends where it began, in a garden with a river and the tree of life. In the new Jerusalem God's servants worship him and see his face. The Gospel shows the way in: Jesus welcomes the little children, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these. Those who come to him like children are the ones who will see God's face.

set: This is the last vision of Revelation, the end of the description of the new Jerusalem coming down from heaven (21:1–22:5). John gathers images from the whole Bible: the river of Eden (Genesis 2:10); the river flowing from the Temple in Ezekiel's vision, with trees whose leaves are for healing (Ezekiel 47:1–12); and the tree of life, guarded after the fall (Genesis 3:22–24).
str: vv. 1–2: the river of the water of life and the tree of life.
vv. 3b–4: the throne, the worship, the face, the name.
v. 5: no more night; the Lord God is their light, and they reign for ever.
kw: The living water Jesus promised (John 4:14; 7:37–39); John explains that he spoke of the Spirit.
Barred to Adam and Eve after the fall, now open again. The Fathers often saw the Cross as the new tree of life.
The curse of Genesis 3:17 is lifted. Nothing will stand between God and his people again.
vv: Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb
One throne for God and the Lamb: the risen Christ shares the Father's throne.
Nothing accursed will be found there any more.
they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.

What Moses was refused (Exodus 33:20) is given to all God's servants. The name on the forehead recalls the gold plate on the high priest's turban, engraved “Holy to the Lord” (Exodus 28:36–38): all the redeemed are priests.
ch: The Catechism calls this contemplation of God in heavenly glory the beatific vision (CCC 1028), and sees in “the river of the water of life” one of the most beautiful symbols of the Holy Spirit, in the heavenly liturgy in which the Church on earth already shares (CCC 1137). Every Holy Qurbana is a sharing in the worship of “his servants” before the throne of God and of the Lamb.

r.h: Let the little children come to me
set: In Matthew this scene stands between Jesus' teaching on marriage (19:3–12) and the rich young man (19:16–22). It was a custom to ask a respected teacher to bless children. The disciples think the Teacher has more important work to do.
str: v. 13: children are brought for the laying on of hands and prayer; the disciples rebuke those who bring them.
kw: Small children, with no status or merit in that society. They bring nothing but their need.
The kingdom belongs not only to children but to all who receive it as children do: as a gift.
vv: Then little children were being brought to him in order that he might lay his hands on them and pray.
The laying on of hands is a gesture of blessing (Genesis 48:14). Matthew says that Jesus did so before he went on his way (19:15).
Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them; for it is to such as these that the kingdom of heaven belongs.
Mark adds that Jesus was indignant with the disciples and took the children up in his arms (Mark 10:14, 16).
ch: The Catechism teaches that to become a child in relation to God is the condition for entering the Kingdom (CCC 526). Jesus' tenderness toward children, shown in these words, allows the Church to hope for children who die without baptism, and makes all the more urgent her call not to keep little children from coming to Christ through baptism (CCC 1250, 1261).

study: Revelation promises that God's servants “will see his face”. How does this hope change the way I face death and loss?
What would it mean for me this week to receive the kingdom like the little children Jesus welcomed?
